# netcup_scp_user_firewall_policy (Resource)

Manages a firewall policy in the netcup SCP account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netcup_scp_user_firewall_policy" "example" {
  user_id = 1234

  name        = "allow-ssh-and-https"
  description = "Managed by Terraform"

  rules = [
    {
      action            = "ACCEPT"
      direction         = "INGRESS"
      protocol          = "TCP"
      destination_ports = "22"
      sources           = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
    },
    {
      action            = "ACCEPT"
      direction         = "INGRESS"
      protocol          = "TCP"
      destination_ports = "443"
      sources           = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Policy name.
- `user_id` (Number) Id of the SCP user account that owns the policy.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Policy description.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Firewall rules, evaluated in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) SCP firewall policy id.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) Firewall action. ACCEPT or DROP.
- `direction` (String) Rule direction. INGRESS or EGRESS.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol. TCP, UDP, ICMP or ICMPv6.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Rule description.
- `destination_ports` (String) Destination port or range.
- `destinations` (List of String) Destination CIDRs/addresses.
- `number_of_effective_rules` (Number) Number of effective rules generated from this rule.
- `source_ports` (String) Source port or range.
- `sources` (List of String) Source CIDRs/addresses.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# terraform import netcup_scp_user_firewall_policy.example 12345/67890
```
